relation_to_prior_protocols.mover-v3-draft-20260924: The archived full draft. This core carries over its H1 and H3 definitions, restricted as item_set states, and the rules it names. The core governs wherever the two differ.

question: Among US-equity extreme daily movers (population D), does MAX lottery conditioning (H1), or the overnight versus intraday split of the hold (H3), change the sign or size of the cost-net forward return? Continuation is one tested outcome, not the premise.
direction: long only (a short side for the MAX-reversal prior is an open question; borrow, hard-to-borrow fees and SEC Rule 201 were not examined)

item_set.family: m = 5: two primary tests that are not tradable (H1-D, H3-c) and three tradable cells (H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b). Holm runs over these five items only.

items.statistic: mean net(b_lane | high MAX21 tercile) - mean net(b_lane | low MAX21 tercile), population D
items.why_kept: The direct test of H1. BCW 2011 predicts that high-MAX names underperform low-MAX names. The high-minus-low difference on one arm is the smallest statistic that tests that prediction. The 5-session b_lane arm is kept because it is the D horizon closest to BCW's holding period.

items.statistic: mean net(b_lane | low MAX21 tercile), population D
items.why_kept: The study is long-only and asks about cost-net returns. The low-MAX tercile is the only H1 cell for which the prior predicts the best relative return, so it is the one cell whose pass would make the conditioning tradable. The high and middle cells (high has a negative prior, middle none) are reported descriptively with no p-value.

The intraday leg as a trade: one regular session, from 09:35 to 15:55 ET on t+1. With H3-b it answers whether either leg is tradable after costs. Neither leg has a mover-specific sourced sign, so both are kept.
The overnight leg as a trade: from 15:55 ET on t+1 to the first eligible quote from 09:30 ET on t+2. It is the counterpart of H3-a.

items.statistic: mean over events of (mean of the 4 overnight leg log returns - mean of the 4 intraday leg log returns), gross, legs as in arms.c_decomposition
items.alternative: not equal to 0 at every stage; at the holdout a pass also needs the sign of the validation estimate (multiple_testing.no_direction_lock)
items.why_kept: The direct test of H3's 'versus'. It uses official prints only, so it needs no fill and no cost model. LPS 2019 uses value-weight portfolios of US stocks priced at least $5 outside the bottom NYSE size quintile (1993-2013, monthly, gross of costs) and has no daily-mover result; its closest analogue, the one-month reversal spread (+0.93%/month overnight and -1.05%/month intraday CAPM alphas, Table 2), is an indirect relative prior at most, so the test is two-sided at every stage. It is not locked to the development sign, because development is survivorship-limited (chronology.labels.development) and gates nothing. At the holdout, a confirmatory pass also needs the holdout estimate to have the sign of the governing validation estimate, so a pass replicates the screened direction.

item_set.tradable_cells: H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a and H3-b are tradable cells and nothing else. H1-D and H3-c are primary tests and are never tradable cells. The robustness requirement (statistics.robustness_required_for_a_pass) applies to the three tradable cells only.
item_set.dropped_from_the_full_draft: Population I and its minute-trigger formulas: it is a second population with its own open finding (the listing-exchange opening print can come after decision minute m), and neither H1 nor H3 needs it. The H1 arms a_fast and c_session and their 12 cells (6 per population): they multiplied cells without adding a test of the conditioning. H1-I and the 9 I-lane cells. The holdout cap of 5 tradable cells: with three tradable cells it has no work to do, so the gate opens for every validated item. The 2017-2019 cost re-measure: it is replaced by the per-fill realized half-spread floor (cost_model.per_side), which removes a pre-outcome stage whose quote stamps were outcome prices. H2, H4 and H5 (and their data gates) and H6: deferred (README appendix).

exposure_registry.consequence: 2017-2020 is exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development (both lanes) and the S2 headline above. Development (2017-2019) and validation (2020) are therefore screening stages only. Validation decides which items the holdout gate opens for, but a validation pass is labelled 'screened', never confirmatory. Only the prospective holdout can support a confirmatory claim. Beside each validation result, the same statistic is reported on the least-exposed slice: symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision (med20 of raw close x volume < $2M, fewer than 60 prior contiguous bars, or has_gap, as broad-universe protocol.json defines them). The slice is a sensitivity, not a separate test.
exposure_registry.update_rule: Every later read of data in any v3 window before the freeze is appended here with its date and purpose. No quote at a planned v3 entry or exit stamp is fetched before the freeze. The coverage-stamp quotes (pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps) are chosen with no reference to event membership and may fall inside a later D trade's hold or terminal-search window; only the count-only code opens them. Daily bars, official prints and quotes are fetched before the freeze only into the sealed pre_freeze_access_path snapshot, whose 2016-2020 screen part is a hashed sample, never the full screen, and are opened only by the count-only code. Any other pre-freeze read is forbidden, not tolerated. If one happens anyway, it is appended here and recorded as a numbered deviation before the freeze, and it voids this protocol version's tests: every item scores p = 1 in the validation Holm run, so the holdout never opens. A read of a v3-defined outcome in the validation window before the freeze voids validation. A read in the holdout window before the gate opens voids the holdout.

pre_freeze_access_path.rule: Before the freeze, data are fetched only by committed count-only code in the study tree (run_discipline.study_code). Raw pages go straight into a private snapshot sealed by sha256. They are never opened by a person or by any other code. The count-only code emits only counts, rates and the coverage_rule decisions: no price, spread, return, gain, covariate value, event list or symbol-level row. Its committed output is the input to the freeze preconditions. Parts 1 and 3 of the pre-freeze snapshot are never inputs of the frozen evaluation; parts 0 and 2 are, as snapshot_part_permissions states (review round 8, F13). Its 2016-2020 screen part is a hashed sample of symbol-sessions, enough for coverage rates and a candidate count, so before the freeze no complete set of inputs to any development or validation outcome (including H3-c's official prints and close-to-close proxies of b_lane) exists on disk while the draft is still editable. The full 2016-2020 screen data and every per-event request are fetched only after the freeze under run_discipline.fetch (review round 7, C4).
pre_freeze_access_path.snapshot_contents: (0) The enumerated symbol list (universe_and_identity.enumeration), with its source responses, and the corporate-action records from 2016-01-01 to the fetch date. (1) A hashed sample of 2016-2020 screen data. The pair (symbol, s) is sampled if int.from_bytes(sha256('mover-v3-sample|' + symbol + '|' + s)[:8], 'big') % 20 == 0, for every enumerated symbol and every XNYS session s from 2016-01-04 to 2020-12-31, with no reference to event membership. For each sampled pair: the daily bars (adjustment raw, split and all) and official prints (auctions, with their sessions_io.official_price source labels) of sessions s-1 and s, requested with asof = s; the same daily bars requested at the provider's default asof, for identity_diagnostic only; and, for the pairs that quote_coverage_stamps selects, the coverage-stamp quotes requested with asof = s. No 2016-2020 screen row outside the sample is fetched before the freeze. (2) The full screen data (as in part 1, for the whole enumerated list, without the default-asof copy) for every session from 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31, sessions of v1/v2 validation that are already exposed, for the holdout breakpoints only (tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints). (3) The native identity probe of identity_probe. No minute bar and no other quote is fetched before the freeze. Every part is pinned by sha256. Each page record keeps its request asof and its fetch date (the vintage) as separate fields.

snapshot_part_permissions.rule: Which snapshot part each reader may open, and for what (review round 8, F13). Only committed code opens a part, never a person. Opening a part outside this table is a forbidden read (exposure_registry.update_rule).
snapshot_part_permissions.part_0: The enumerated symbol list and the corporate-action records. Before the freeze: the snapshot fetch code (to request parts 1-3) and the count-only code (per-source and per-year counts). After the freeze: an input of the frozen evaluation, pinned by its sha256 in freeze_record. The full 2016-2020 screen fetch enumerates from it, and identity (universe_and_identity.dedup), the in-hold record rules, the cash entitlements (populations.corporate_actions) and the terminal-merger booking read its records for 2016-2020.
snapshot_part_permissions.part_1: The 2016-2020 hashed sample. The count-only code only, before the freeze. Never an input of the frozen evaluation: the full screen is fetched after the freeze (run_discipline.fetch).
snapshot_part_permissions.part_2: The 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 screen data. Unopened before the freeze. After the freeze: an input of the frozen evaluation for holdout breakpoint membership only (tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints), opened under the first granted 'count' entry. It supplies no outcome.
snapshot_part_permissions.part_3: The identity probe. The count-only code only, before the freeze. Never an input of the frozen evaluation.

pre_freeze_access_path.outputs: From the part-1 sample, per calendar year and listing exchange (sampled counts, and rates where coverage_rule names them): symbol-sessions with a daily bar; with a raw close >= $1; with each official_price source label for the open and the close (populations.official_prints); with a suspected unadjusted split at s (populations.suspected_unadjusted_split); and candidates, the sampled symbol-sessions that pass the gain condition, the $1 floor, the suspected-split rule and exclusions 1 and 2 (a count only: no DV_reg, no price and no symbol; review round 7, C8). From part 0, per year: split, reverse-split, cash-dividend and merger records, and enumerated symbols per source. Also the coverage-stamp quote counts (quote_coverage_stamps), screen requests answered with no row (universe_and_identity.empty_responses), the counts of identity_diagnostic and identity_probe, and each year's coverage_rule rates with the kept or dropped decision and the item_rule result, computed by the count-only code itself (coverage_rule.decided_by_code). The snapshot fetch code also writes a transport log per request kind and API (requests, pages, bytes, HTTP statuses, retries and timings; no data value), the throughput evidence of freeze_preconditions[5] (review round 8, F12).
pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps: Eligible-quote rates are measured only at stamps that are never planned v3 entry or exit stamps: 12:17 ET and 14:43 ET (12:17 and 12:43 ET on a 13:00 early close). They may fall inside a later D trade's hold or terminal-search window; only the count-only code opens them. The symbol-sessions are selected among the part-1 sampled symbol-sessions with a daily bar and a raw close >= $1 by int.from_bytes(sha256('mover-v3-coverage|' + symbol + '|' + session)[:8], 'big') % 25 == 0 (about 1 in 500 overall), with no reference to event membership. A stamp has an eligible quote if the NBBO prevailing at the stamp is eligible (populations.fill_quote) and at most 1000 ms old, or if the first eligible quote update after the stamp arrives within 60 s. Per year, the code reports the stamps with an eligible quote, those without one, and those that are fetch-incomplete (populations.fetch_failures), and nothing else.
pre_freeze_access_path.runs: The count-only code runs once, from the committed study tree named in its output. Every run, including a failed or partial one, is appended to exposure_registry.run_entries with its revision, tree, date, status, output sha256, spec_sha256 and input_manifest_sha256 (coverage_rule.decided_by_code). A rerun is allowed only after a failed or incomplete run, and never after its rates were read. The first complete run's output governs coverage_rule and the identity probe, and its bindings govern the freeze (review round 8, F04). The count-only code is the only code that opens parts 1 and 3 (snapshot_part_permissions).
pre_freeze_access_path.not_allowed: No pre-freeze fetch or read of a quote at a planned D entry or exit stamp. No pre-freeze fetch of 2016-2020 screen rows outside the part-1 sample. No opening of the sealed snapshot's bars, prints or quotes by a person or by code other than the count-only code. No computation of D membership (the candidate count stops before DV_reg), MAX21 or any outcome.
pre_freeze_access_path.identity_diagnostic: A count-only measure of what asof = s screening cannot reach (review round 7, F4). A part-1 sampled pair (X, s) is identity-unreached if X's default-asof response has a daily bar for s with a raw close >= $1 whose raw OHLCV differs from X's asof = s row, or X has no asof = s row, and no retained name_change record names X as its new symbol. Such a history belongs to an issuer that carried another ticker on s, and asof = s screening reaches it only through that old ticker, which neither enumeration source holds when no rename record was retained. broad-universe, which requested the default asof, received such histories under the successor ticker. Per year, the code reports the sampled pairs with a default-asof bar and raw close >= $1, the identity-unreached pairs and their rate, and the distinct unreached symbols. The rate is an upper bound (an old ticker can still be in the asset master). It enters coverage_rule.year_rule and chronology.labels.validation.
pre_freeze_access_path.identity_probe: A count-only native check of the asof = t behaviour that universe_and_identity.asof relies on, for 2016-2020 (review round 7, F5). The list is fixed by rule: every name_change record of part 0 effective on a session d from 2016-01-04 to 2020-12-31 (old symbol O, new symbol N), ordered by sha256('mover-v3-probe|' + O + '|' + N + '|' + d) and capped at the first 100. For each, the code requests O with asof = d-3 and N with asof = d+3 (sessions), each over sessions d-3 .. d+3, for daily bars (raw), auctions and quotes (the 60 s ending 12:17 ET on d-1 and on d+1). Records are normalized before comparison: daily bars by XNYS session date (the bar timestamp in America/New_York) with raw open, high, low, close and volume as returned; auction prints by session date, auction kind (opening or closing), exchange, price and size; quotes by timestamp to the nanosecond, bid and ask price, size and exchange. A rename probe matches on bars, or on auctions, if the two responses have at least 5 common sessions with a normalized record, at least 2 before d and 2 on or after d, and identical normalized records on every common session; on quotes, if both 60 s windows are non-empty in both responses and their normalized records are identical. A probe with less overlap is insufficient, counted, and scored as a mismatch (review round 8, F09). Ticker reuse is probed on every symbol that is the old symbol of one name_change record and the new symbol of a later one inside 2016-2020 (same order, capped at 50): requested for a session before the first record, once with asof before the first record and once with asof after the second, the two responses must both be non-empty (else the probe is insufficient and fails) and differ in raw OHLCV. Only match and mismatch counts per endpoint are emitted. The freeze needs at least 20 rename probes, at least 95% matches for bars and for auctions and at least 90% for quotes; otherwise the protocol is not frozen as written. Ticker reuse is verified if at least 5 reuse probes exist and at least 90% of them differ; otherwise (no case, too few, or failing) it is unresolved. Unresolved reuse: every development and validation D event whose as-known symbol is such a reused symbol is excluded from every primary statistic and counted per stage (restoring them is a sensitivity), and those results carry the qualifier 'identity-limited (ticker reuse unresolved)' (review round 8, F09).

universe_and_identity.enumeration: The symbol list for 2016-2020 and for the 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 breakpoint sessions is the union of two sources. (a) The Alpaca asset master: GET /v2/assets with status=active and with status=inactive, class us_equity, every current exchange including OTC (today's OTC listing says nothing about 2016-2020 listing, which exclusions rule 1 decides from session data). Symbols that fail collect_daily.py DATA_SYMBOL at aa6fc79 (CUSIP-style placeholders the bars API rejects) are removed. (b) Every old and new symbol named by an Alpaca corporate-action record (GET /v1/corporate-actions, every action type, 2016-01-01 to the fetch date). This is broad-universe's supplement method (collect_daily.py and corporate_actions.py at aa6fc79), except that renamed-away tickers are kept, because per-session asof resolves them. The list is written once, sealed with the pre-freeze snapshot and pinned by sha256, and its per-source counts are count-only outputs. Survivorship limit: a name delisted in 2016-2019 that is absent from both sources cannot be discovered (broad-universe/README.md: 'names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained action cannot be discovered from entitled sources'), so development keeps the survivorship-limited label. A second limit concerns identity: an issuer renamed without a retained name_change record, whose old ticker is in neither source, is not reached for its pre-rename sessions by asof = s screening, although broad-universe, which requested the provider's default asof, received that history under the successor ticker (113 of its 155 duplicate pairs were resolved without a rename record, and name_change records number 57 for 2017-2019; broad-universe/README.md). exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.identity_diagnostic measures it per year, and coverage_rule.year_rule and chronology.labels.validation use it. Holdout collection batches enumerate from the same two sources, refreshed at each batch, united with every earlier batch's list.
universe_and_identity.asof: Every request for bars, auctions (official prints) or quotes carries Alpaca's asof parameter set to a session date, never to the fetch date and never to the provider default. A screen request for session s uses asof = s. Every request for a D event decided on session t uses the event's as-known symbol with asof = t. The as-known symbol is the one under which the event appeared in the asof = t screen. Such requests cover the event's daily bars (raw, split and all) from t-22 through the end of its terminal-search window, its minute bars, its entry, exit and terminal-search quotes and its official prints through the end of its hold or search window. A rename inside a hold or lookback is therefore resolved to the same issuer. The fetch date is kept as a separate vintage field in each page record. quotes.py fetch_one, whose PROTOCOL_ASOF is fixed at '2026-09-21', is never called.

availability.rule: What each decision input may contain, and from which vintage (review round 8, F08). asof = t fixes the symbol's identity, not the information vintage. An input may use only data stamped before its decision time; for the holdout, only data the collector sealed within one session of the decision; for development and validation, every input is a retrospective reconstruction from the provider's history as fetched after the freeze.
availability.membership: Official prints of t and t-1 stamped before 16:15 ET on t (a closing print stamped later is a missing close: no event, counted); the daily bars of t-1 and t for f(t) and the suspected-split rule; DV_reg from the 1-minute bars of t that start before the scheduled close.
availability.lookbacks: MAX21 from the official prints and daily bars of t-22 .. t-1; med20 and sigma_d from W(t), sessions t-19 .. t; tercile breakpoints from the MAX21 of earlier D events only (tercile_rule).
availability.entry_time: The entry bar and the cost tier's cum_dv from 1-minute bars complete at the fill-decision time X (populations.formulas).
availability.identity: Corporate-action records effective on or before the decision session, and dedup as universe_and_identity.dedup restricts it; the current asset-master status is never an input.
availability.vintage_development_validation: Retrospective reconstruction. Every input is the provider's history as fetched after the freeze (the fetch date is each page's vintage), so it can contain later corrections, late-reported trades and backfilled records that were not observable at the decision, and record completeness before 2020 is limited (universe_and_identity.enumeration). Revision exposure is not measured. Every development and validation result carries the qualifier 'retrospective reconstruction' (outcome_reporting.qualifiers) and claims only what the fetched history shows.
availability.vintage_holdout: Prospective capture. The collector seals, in the batch that covers session s, the decision inputs of the D events decided on s (holdout_gate.prospective_collection), and the next batch seals their entry session's 1-minute bars. Holdout decisions use only these sealed captures, never a later re-fetch, so no correction after the capture enters. A ratio of factors (F, f(j), a(s) or q(s)) combines rows of one response and vintage only: decision-time factors from the capture, and hold factors from the one hold-period request per adjustment, so a split announced between the capture and the hold-period fetch cannot enter a ratio. Stated exceptions: a late-collected session (its vintage is the late batch, and trades spanning it are paper-exposed), and the retrospective 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 breakpoint inputs of tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints (snapshot part 2 and the per-event lookbacks fetched under the first 'count').

universe_and_identity.request_shapes: The screen data are: for 2016-2020, the full screen fetch made after the freeze (run_discipline.fetch: daily bars raw, split and all, and official prints of sessions s-1 and s for the whole enumerated list, with asof = s, sealed and pinned before any outcome); for 2024-11 to 2025-12, pre-freeze snapshot part 2; and for the holdout, the collection batches. The pre-freeze sample is never a screen input. The gain condition (close[t], ref(t), f(t)), the $1 floor, suspected unadjusted splits at t and exclusions 1 and 2 are evaluated on the screen data. Only the symbol-sessions that pass them are candidates, and only candidates have per-event data fetched, with the as-known symbol and asof = t. Per-event data are: the minute bars for DV_reg (the last membership condition), med20, the entry bar and cum_dv; the event's daily bars with adjustment raw, split and all, one request per adjustment, from t-22 through the scheduled close of the 5th session after its latest planned exit session (for a censored trade, after the segment's last session; populations.terminal_exits); the official prints over the same sessions; and quotes. The per-event daily bars supply MAX21, exclusion 3, every in-hold share factor and the q(s) distribution check (populations.corporate_actions; the cash term comes from records), each computed within that event's responses only; screen rows, fetched under other symbols, asof values and vintages, are never joined into a per-event computation (review round 7, F1). If a per-event official close of t or t-1 differs from the screen value, the screen value governs membership, and the difference is counted per stage.
universe_and_identity.dedup: Before membership, coverage.dedupe_identity at aa6fc79 (DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SESSIONS = 20, DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SPAN_COVERAGE = 0.98, survivor ranking by retained rename record, then price continuity, then active status, then lexicographic order) is applied, for the events of session s, to the screen rows of the up to 252 sessions ending at s (each from its asof request), with rename_pairs from the retained name_change records effective on or before s and active_symbols empty. The survivor ranking therefore never uses the current asset-master status and falls through to the lexicographic order, and every dedup input is information of sessions up to s (review round 8, F09). There is also a same-session guard. Two candidate D events on one session whose raw daily OHLCV (volume > 0) is identical on both s-1 and s are one event, kept under the higher-ranked symbol. Because the rows are identical, the choice cannot change any price. Pairs removed by either rule are counted per stage. The records' own completeness is retrospective (universe_and_identity.availability).
universe_and_identity.empty_responses: HTTP 200 with no row is an empty response, never silently dropped, and never fetch-incomplete (fetch-incomplete is reserved for HTTP errors and timeouts, populations.fetch_failures). Per stage, the counts reported are: enumerated symbols with no bar in the stage; screen requests with no row; and, per item, event requests with no row. Each empty event request has a fixed consequence. An empty entry-quote window is a no-entry. An empty exit or search window is a terminal exit (populations.terminal_exits), which stays in the statistic. An empty official-print response is a missing print: no event at t, or a missing H3-c leg. An empty lookback makes MAX21 undefined, so the event is unassigned.
universe_and_identity.tests: Synthetic tests with a recorded fake client cover: FB/META (a renamed-away ticker served with its successor's history under both symbols gives one event, not two); a ticker reused by a new issuer after a delisting (asof = t resolves the old issuer); a rename inside a 5-session hold (the as-known symbol with asof = t returns the whole hold); a split and a rename inside the same hold (the share factor comes from the per-event responses under the as-known symbol, never from screen rows, and the cash from the held issuer's records, including a dividend recorded under the successor symbol); an empty exit response (a terminal exit, counted); a request built with the fetch date as asof (refused); dedup at s ignoring rows after s and the asset-master status; and a closing print stamped after 16:15 ET (a missing close).

populations.D_daily: Symbol-sessions t with split-consistent official-close gain close[t]/ref(t) - 1 >= 0.20 - 1e-9, where close[t] is the accepted official close of populations.official_prints and ref(t) is as populations.formulas states. They also need an official close >= $1.00 and a regular-session dollar volume DV_reg(t) >= $1,000,000. A session without an accepted official close is not an event and is counted; there is no bar fallback. The decision is at 16:15 ET on t. Entry is at the first eligible quote at or after 09:35 ET on t+1 (and at or after decision + 60 s), with an entry timeout of 300 s; otherwise there is no entry, and it is counted. The b_overnight entry is the exception (arms.b_overnight).
populations.formulas: Restated exactly, so membership does not depend on unpinned code. Let a(s) = raw daily close(s) / split-adjusted daily close(s), the cumulative split factor of session s, from the daily bars with adjustment=raw and adjustment=split. For sessions u < v, the share factor F(u, v) = a(u) / a(v), set to 1 when |F - 1| <= 1e-2. F(u, v) is undefined if u or v has no daily bar in either adjustment, and every quantity that uses an undefined F is undefined (counted). F telescopes, so a split that takes effect on a session with no bar (for example, halted all day) is still carried between the surrounding sessions with bars. f(j) = F(j-1, j) for consecutive XNYS sessions. Hold accounting uses F only through F_acc (review round 8, F01). R(u, v) is the product, over the held issuer's retained forward_split and reverse_split records (populations.corporate_actions) effective on a session j with u < j <= v, of new_rate / old_rate (R = 1 when there is none). For u <= v, let v' be the latest session in [u, v] with a daily bar in both adjustments. F*(u, v) = R(u, v') if |F(u, v') / R(u, v') - 1| <= 1e-2, which includes the snap to 1 when no record exists; F*(u, v) = F(u, v') if no such record exists and F(u, v') is not within 1e-2 of 1 (a split the bars carry and no record names, counted); otherwise F*(u, v) is undefined (a recorded split the bars do not carry at its ratio: the in-hold rule of populations.suspected_unadjusted_split). F_acc(u, v) = F*(u, v) x R(v', v), so records carry a split past the last session with bars, and F_acc(u, u) = 1. F_acc is undefined if u has no daily bar in both adjustments or F* is undefined. For a delayed exit at a session x after the planned exit session E, F_acc(e, x) = F_acc(e, E) x R(E, x): after E, shares follow records only, so no bar after E can make a trade undefined. q(s) = all-adjusted daily close(s) / split-adjusted daily close(s), the provider's cumulative distribution factor of session s (like a(s), a ratio of two closes of one session, never a return). This is rules.split_factor's arithmetic at aa6fc79 with two deliberate departures: adjustment=split closes replace adjustment=all closes (with adjustment=all, a cash dividend of about 1% or more would be booked as a share change), and a missing input makes F undefined instead of 1 (a default of 1 left a split on a session without a bar unbooked, review round 7 F2). ref(t) = the accepted official close of the previous XNYS session / f(t). If that session has no accepted official close, or f(t) is undefined, ref(t) is undefined and t is not an event (counted). DV_reg(t) = the summed vwap x volume of the 1-minute SIP bars of session t that start at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close (session_calendar); a session with no such bar has DV_reg 0. The split-consistent official-close return of session j is r(j) = C(j) x f(j) / C(j-1) - 1, where C is the accepted official close; r(j) is undefined if either close is missing or f(j) is undefined. MAX21(t) = the maximum over k = 1..21 of r(t-k). These are the 21 returns of sessions t-21 .. t-1, from the 22 accepted official closes of sessions t-22 .. t-1 (the event's own session t is not in the window). If any of those closes is missing, or any session t-21 .. t-1 is a suspected unadjusted split, MAX21 is undefined and the event is unassigned (counted); there is no maximum over fewer returns. The sizing window W(t) is the 20 sessions ending at t (its close is known at the 16:15 decision). med20 = the median of DV_reg over W(t). sigma_d = the sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of log(1 + r(j)) over the 20 sessions j of W(t). If any DV_reg or r(j) in W(t) is undefined, the trade cannot be sized and is a counted no-fill. The entry bar is the last 1-minute SIP bar of the entry session (from 04:00 ET) that is complete at the fill-decision time X, meaning it starts at or before X - 60 s. If there is none, the entry-bar cap is 0 and the trade is a counted no-fill. cum_dv(X) = the summed vwap x volume of the session's 1-minute SIP bars from 04:00 ET that are complete at X, meaning bar start + 60 s <= X, the entry bar's rule (review round 8, F02). It replaces rules.py Bars.cum_dv, which also sums the unfinished bar that contains X. A synthetic test fixes each formula, including a split day, a missing previous close, a missing close inside the MAX21 window, a suspected unadjusted split inside it, a reverse split on a session with no daily bar inside a lookback (MAX21 undefined) and inside a hold (carried by F between the surrounding bars), an entry with no completed bar, F_acc with and without a matching split record, a recorded split the bars do not carry (excluded), a split on an exit session after the last bar (carried by R), a delayed exit across a recorded split, q across a dividend and a spin-off, and cum_dv for a fill exactly at a minute boundary (that bar counts), 1 ms before it and inside a minute (the unfinished bar does not).
populations.official_prints: The accepted source labels of sessions_io.official_price at aa6fc79 are these. The listing exchange is the exchange of the largest condition-O opening print; a session with no O print has no listing exchange. Official open: opening_print_listing_exchange only. Official close: closing_print_listing_exchange or official_close_listing_exchange only. A closing_print_other_exchange, or a session with no O print, counts as no official close and is counted per year. The same rule applies to close[t], to the previous close in ref(t) and to every H3-c leg. For D, the O print of session t precedes the 16:15 ET decision by construction. The synthetic suite has one case per source label, including the rejected label and a session with a closing print but no opening print.
populations.suspected_unadjusted_split: Applied at t before membership, on the screen data. For session t, let r = raw daily close[t] / raw daily close of the previous XNYS session. Session t is a suspected unadjusted split if f(t) = 1 and |r - n| <= 0.01 x n or |r - 1/n| <= 0.01 / n for some integer n in 2..100. Such a session is not an event, and any event whose MAX21 window (t-21 .. t-1) contains a suspected session is unassigned; both are counted per stage. The rule also removes genuine moves at t within 1% of an integer multiple (for example +100%); that loss is preregistered and counted, not corrected. Inside a hold the ratio rule is never applied to a primary statistic: hold-period close ratios are outcomes, and the rule would drop real tail moves of low-priced movers (+100%, +200%, -50%, -67%). A trade is excluded from the primary statistics only on price-independent evidence: F*(e, E) undefined (populations.formulas), meaning a retained forward_split or reverse_split record effective on a session j with e < j <= E' (E' the latest session in [e, E] with bars) whose ratio the adjusted bars do not carry, |F(e, E') / R(e, E') - 1| > 1e-2; for H3-c, the same test on each overnight leg (review round 8, F01). That exclusion uses only records and the cumulative factors a(s) (ratios of two closes of one session, never a return), so count_unit applies it too; it is counted per item and stage. Removing trades whose hold spans a session flagged by the ratio rule is a sensitivity only (statistics.sensitivities; review round 7, C3).
populations.exclusions: (1) Not exchange-listed on the session: a symbol-session is eligible only if it has a listing exchange under populations.official_prints, so OTC-only trading is excluded by as-known session data. The current Alpaca asset exchange and tradable flags are never used. (2) Warrants, units and rights: exclude the symbol if (len(symbol) == 5 and re.search('[A-Z]{4}[WUR]$', symbol)) or re.search('\.(WS|U|R|W)', symbol) (Python re, unanchored search), which is candidates.py's rule at aa6fc79 (its SQL regexp_matches, line 47), or if the symbol contains '/', a v3 addition that candidates.py does not have. (3) Symbols with fewer than 21 prior XNYS sessions with a daily bar. Each exclusion is counted per stage, with a synthetic test per rule. There is no halt exclusion (halts).
populations.fetch_failures: The frozen fetch code is v3-owned and lives in the study tree. It writes page and stamp records in quotes.py's format at aa6fc79. Every request is retried up to 3 times, with waits of 1 s, 4 s and 16 s. A request that still fails with an HTTP error, a URLError or a timeout makes its stamp fetch-incomplete (a stamp_incomplete record). The run continues and does not raise. The trade that needs the stamp is excluded, not counted as a no-entry or a terminal exit, and the count is reported per item. If more than 1% of the stamps a stage requires are fetch-incomplete after the single re-fetch of run_discipline.fetch, that stage is void: every item scores p = 1 and is labelled underpowered there, with the reason stated. The rate is committed before any outcome of the stage, and a void is final. Synthetic tests cover an exhausted URLError and a timeout (each becomes stamp_incomplete, and the pool run completes), a success on the third retry, and an empty response (not fetch-incomplete).
populations.session_calendar: XNYS from exchange_calendars 4.13.2 (the version rules.py used for 2021-2026), for 2016-01-01 through the end of the last possible holdout extension. The session list, with each session's scheduled open and close, is written to the v3 data file data/session-calendar.json and pinned by sha256 at the freeze (run_discipline.data_files). A 'session' anywhere in this protocol is every scheduled XNYS trading session, early closes included. The pinned file cannot know about unscheduled future closures, such as a national day of mourning. Such a closure is removed only by a line in data/session-calendar-amendments.jsonl that cites its primary source (an NYSE notice) in the format of run_discipline.amendment_format, is committed and pushed, and is logged in the access log (purpose 'amend') before the affected session. It may concern only a date on or after the freeze session. The freeze session and N0 keep the dates computed at the freeze, and if N0 itself closes, the holdout starts at the next session. The 252-session holdout and each 63-session block count actual sessions. Synthetic tests use the 2017-07-03, 2017-11-24, 2018-11-23, 2019-12-24 and 2020-11-27 early closes and a removed session inside the holdout.
populations.session_times: Every '15:55 ET' in this protocol means the scheduled close (session_calendar) minus 5 minutes (12:55 ET on a 13:00 early close). Eligible quotes are regular-session quotes, at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close. D decisions stay at 16:15 ET on early-close sessions.
populations.fill_quote: For a fill at or after time X, the quote is the NBBO prevailing at X (the latest quote update stamped at or before X) if it is eligible and X minus its timestamp is at most 1000 ms. Otherwise it is the first eligible quote update stamped after X, with the fill time equal to its timestamp. Eligible means bid > 0 and ask > bid (locked and crossed quotes excluded, as quotes.py valid_quote at aa6fc79 does; its pinned copy is applied only as a predicate to one quote at a time, never to a quote list, where it would skip newer locked or crossed quotes and return an older one) and regular session (session_times). Timeouts run from X. Synthetic tests cover a fresh prevailing quote, a stale one, a locked one and no quote inside the timeout.
populations.fill_price: Every entry and non-terminal exit fills at the mid (bid + ask) / 2 of the eligible quote that fills it, so gross returns are mid to mid. cost_model.per_side adds the per-side cost on top.

terminal_exits.search_window: An exit fills at the first eligible quote at or after its planned stamp. If none arrives before the scheduled close, the search continues session by session through the scheduled close of the 5th XNYS session after the planned exit session E (E+5). For a trade censored at a segment end, E is the segment's last session (segment_end). A fill inside the window is a normal exit, flagged delayed and counted.
terminal_exits.terminal: A held position with no eligible quote in its search window is terminal. This covers a delisting, a move to OTC-only trading (outside the SIP NBBO), an SEC trading suspension, a halt that does not resume inside the window, and an exit request answered empty (universe_and_identity.empty_responses).
terminal_exits.booking: Terminal-merger: if a retained corporate-action record of type cash_merger, stock_merger or stock_and_cash_merger names the held as-known symbol as the acquiree (its acquiree symbol field) and is effective on a session from the entry session through the end of the search window, the exit is booked at the last eligible bid of the hold. That is the bid of the latest eligible quote stamped at or after the entry fill quote's timestamp and at or before the planned exit stamp; the entry fill quote itself qualifies, so the bid always exists (review round 8, F05), and merger arbitrage keeps it near the consideration. Fees are charged on that raw bid, with no further spread cost and no impact (populations.corporate_actions gives the formula). A record in which the held symbol is only the acquirer does not qualify. Terminal-zero: every other terminal trade is booked at an exit value of 0, a total loss of the position, with no exit fees. This is the stated choice. Booking at the last eligible bid for all terminal trades is a sensitivity only. Corporate-action records are thin before 2020 (broad-universe/README.md), so a merger without a retained record books terminal-zero; per stage and year, terminal-zero trades with no merger record of any kind for the symbol are reported beside the merger-record counts.
terminal_exits.in_statistics: Terminal trades stay in every primary statistic, in count_unit and in the minimum samples. For each item and stage, the counts of delayed, terminal-merger and terminal-zero exits are reported. H3-c has no position: an event whose hold loses a leg this way lacks its 8 legs, is excluded from H3-c, and is counted as terminal in H3-c's report.
terminal_exits.segment_end: A trade censored at a segment end (chronology.boundaries) exits at the first eligible quote at or after its censoring stamp, 15:55 ET on the segment's last session. If none arrives before that session's scheduled close, the search continues past the segment end under the normal rule, through the scheduled close of the 5th XNYS session after the segment's last session, with the event's as-known symbol and asof = t. Quotes after the segment end are this trade's exit data only; they create no entry and no event. A fill there is flagged censored-delayed. With no eligible quote by then, the trade is terminal under the same booking and flagged censored-terminal. Where a segment ends therefore never by itself books a -100% (review round 7, C11).
terminal_exits.tests: Synthetic tests: a delisting inside a 5-session hold (terminal-zero); a delisting on a segment's last session (censored-terminal); a censored trade whose first eligible quote comes on the session after the segment end (censored-delayed); a halt that resumes on E+3 (delayed exit); a halt that has not resumed by E+5 (terminal-zero); a cash merger effective inside the hold (terminal-merger at the last eligible bid); a terminal merger with no eligible quote after the entry fill (booked at the entry fill quote's bid); an empty exit response; and a check that each case is counted and kept in the statistic.

populations.corporate_actions: Distributions are booked from corporate-action entitlements (review round 8, F01). Deviation D7's method (evaluate_v2.py lines 416-420 at aa6fc79) booked cash as the residual raw_c(e) x all_c(x) / all_c(e) - F x raw_c(x) with a 1e-4 clamp. That residual moves with the exit session's close, so an overnight leg ending at open(x) changed with close(x), and adjustment=all also carries spin-offs, which it booked as cash. v3 keeps D7's share-factor structure and replaces its cash term. Let e be the entry session and x the exit session (the session of the exit fill, or of the terminal-merger bid), E the planned exit session, and N = filled notional / entry mid the entry shares. The held issuer's records are the retained corporate-action records (pre-freeze snapshot part 0 for 2016-2020, the collection batches for the holdout) whose symbol is the as-known symbol, or a successor symbol that a retained name_change record effective on a session from e through x maps it to. Every price input comes from the event's per-event daily-bar and official-print responses (universe_and_identity.request_shapes), never from screen rows. Shares: exit shares are N x F_acc(e, x) (populations.formulas). Cash: per original share, cash = the sum, over the held issuer's cash_dividend records with ex-date j and e < j <= x, of the record's per-share rate x F_acc(e, j - 1); special dividends are included, booked gross at the ex-date and not reinvested. No price enters the cash term. Non-cash distributions: a spin_off, stock_dividend, rights_distribution or unit_split record of the held issuer effective on a session j with e < j <= E excludes the trade (for H3-c, t+1 < j <= t+5 excludes the event); the distributed asset is never valued. Unrecorded distributions: a session j with e < j <= E (for H3-c, t+1 < j <= t+5) where j - 1 and j both have daily bars in the split and all adjustments, |q(j - 1) / q(j) - 1| > 5e-3 (0.5%, a design choice above the provider's price rounding), and no cash_dividend or non-cash distribution record of the held issuer has ex-date j excludes the trade or event; booking it with no cash is a sensitivity. These exclusions and the split mismatch of populations.suspected_unadjusted_split use only records, a(s) and q(s), so count_unit applies them, and each is counted per item and stage. After E (a delayed exit, E < x) nothing excludes: shares follow F_acc, a cash_dividend record adds its cash, and a non-cash or unrecorded distribution is booked at zero value and counted. For a same-session trade or leg (an a_intraday trade exited on its entry session, each intraday H3-c leg) e = x, so F_acc = 1 and cash = 0. The trade net return is net = (N x F_acc(e, x) x exit_mid x (1 - c_out) - sell_fees + N x cash) / (N x entry_mid x (1 + c_in)) - 1, where c_in and c_out are the entry and exit costs of cost_model.per_side (fractions of the mid, impact included) and sell_fees is the dollar SEC Section 31 fee and FINRA TAF on selling N x F_acc(e, x) shares at the raw exit mid (cost_model.fees; no fee on the buy, and commission 0). A terminal-merger exit uses exit_mid = the last eligible bid (populations.terminal_exits.booking) and c_out = 0, with fees on that bid. A terminal-zero trade has net = -1 exactly (no exit value, fees or cash). H3-c legs are gross: an overnight leg is log((raw official open(x) x F_acc(e, x) + cash) / raw official close(e)) with e = t+k and x = t+k+1, and an intraday leg is log(raw official close / raw official open) of one session. An undefined F_acc excludes the trade, or the H3-c event, and is counted. Mergers follow populations.terminal_exits. Accounting identity: for every arm and each overnight H3-c leg, replacing every price stamped after the trade's exit fill or the leg's endpoint (the close of x, and later sessions' bars and prints, raw, split and all-adjusted consistently) leaves the booked return unchanged. Synthetic tests, passed before the freeze, fix the net-return formula on a small table, assert that identity, and cross a split with and without a record, an ordinary ex-dividend date, a 5% special cash dividend (booked as cash with F_acc = 1, never as a share change, and not a suspected unadjusted split), a dividend whose ex-date is the exit session of b_overnight and of an overnight H3-c leg, a split effective on that exit session, a split and a dividend in one hold (the rate applied to the post-split shares), a dividend recorded under a successor symbol, a spin-off record inside the hold (excluded), an unrecorded distribution (excluded) and a spin-off between E and a delayed exit (booked at zero).
populations.halts: No halt source is used, historically or prospectively, so no trade set depends on a later data purchase. As in catalyst-experiment, a halt is never inferred from missing data. An entry fills only at an eligible quote, and an entry with none inside its timeout is a counted no-entry. An exit waits for an eligible quote and becomes terminal after its search window (populations.terminal_exits). Limitation: a trade that sits through a short unobserved halt is not flagged.
populations.parameter_provenance: G = 0.20 and V = $1M are v1's loosest gain and middle volume floor. They were fixed for sample size after v1's all-negative dev/val grid was seen (a disclosed exposure) and are not tuned on any v3 window.

arms.b_lane: H1: entry as D_daily; exit at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the 5th holding session (the entry session t+1 is holding session 1), under populations.terminal_exits
arms.a_intraday: H3-a: entry as D_daily (09:35 ET on t+1, timeout 300 s); exit at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the entry session. Its entries are the b_lane entries of all D events, assigned or unassigned to a tercile. The overlap is intended and reported.
arms.b_overnight: H3-b: entry at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on t+1, timeout 300 s; otherwise no entry (counted). Exit at the first eligible quote at or after 09:30 ET on t+2, under populations.terminal_exits
arms.c_decomposition: H3-c, diagnostic only, not traded, gross, from official prints only: over sessions t+1 .. t+5 of every D event (no entry fill needed), the overnight legs k = 1..4 run from the official close of t+k to the official open of t+k+1, and the intraday legs k = 2..5 run from the official open to the official close of t+k. The partial first-session leg is excluded, so each event has 4 legs of each kind, and together they decompose official close(t+1) to official close(t+5). Overnight legs carry the share factor and cash entitlement of populations.corporate_actions (F_acc and the cash_dividend records with ex-date t+k+1), so no leg depends on a price after its endpoint. An event with a split mismatch, a non-cash or an unrecorded distribution in t+2 .. t+5, or with no daily bar in both adjustments on a session from t+1 to t+4 (the start of an overnight leg), is excluded and counted (review round 8, F01 and F05). An event missing any of the 8 legs is excluded from H3-c and counted; no bar or quote substitutes, and no event is averaged over fewer legs.
arms.stops_and_sizing: No stops. Research sizing is 1x equal notional, capacity-capped (cost_model.fix_2_impact_and_capacity).

coverage_rule.scope: All five items, with one set of kept years per stage. It is decided at the freeze from the count-only outputs (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path), before any outcome, and recorded in freeze_record with multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze.
coverage_rule.no_fallback: A session or symbol without an accepted official print or an eligible quote stays a counted non-event, no-entry, terminal or excluded trade under its own rule. No bar, quote or other-exchange substitute is ever used.
coverage_rule.year_rule: A calendar year y of 2016-2020 is dropped from its stage entirely (every session of that year) if any of these holds, each from the part-1 sample (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path). Each rate has one denominator cohort and a numerator that is a subset of it (review round 8, F03). (a) Official close: cohort A_y = the sampled symbol-sessions (X, s) of y whose raw daily bar of s (asof = s) exists with raw close >= $1; numerator = the members of A_y with an accepted official close of s (populations.official_prints). A member whose auctions request is fetch-incomplete stays in A_y and counts against coverage. A sampled pair whose raw daily-bar request is fetch-incomplete cannot be placed and is counted as cohort-undetermined; if cohort-undetermined pairs exceed 1% of y's sampled pairs, rate (a) is unavailable. The year fails (a) if the rate is below 90% or unavailable. (b) Eligible quote: cohort Q_y = the coverage stamps of y (quote_coverage_stamps, both stamps of each selected symbol-session, selected from A_y); numerator = the stamps of Q_y with an eligible quote, so a stamp without one and a fetch-incomplete stamp count against coverage. The year fails (b) if the rate is below 80%. (c) Identity: cohort I_y = the sampled pairs of y with a default-asof daily bar of s with raw close >= $1 (identity_diagnostic); numerator = the identity-unreached pairs of I_y, and a pair whose asof = s request is fetch-incomplete counts as unreached. The year fails (c) if the rate is above 10%. Fail-closed: an empty cohort, or a rate that is unavailable, fails its condition, so an undefined rate never keeps a year. Comparisons are exact integer comparisons (the year fails (a) if 100 x numerator < 90 x |A_y|, (b) if 100 x numerator < 80 x |Q_y|, (c) if 100 x numerator > 10 x |I_y|), so a rate exactly at its threshold passes. If 2016, the warm-up year, is dropped, events of early 2017 stay unassigned under tercile_rule.minimum until 60 prior events accrue. The thresholds are design choices, not measured values. Synthetic boundary cases: each rate exactly at, one unit below and one unit above its threshold; an empty cohort; cohort-undetermined pairs at exactly 1% and just above; a fetch-incomplete auctions request, stamp and asof = s request; and an accepted close on a pair with no daily bar or a raw close below $1, which is not counted, so no rate can exceed 100%.
coverage_rule.item_rule: If 2020 is dropped, no item is tested: all 5 items score p = 1 at validation and the holdout, permanently, and that is the recorded result of this protocol version. Development years do not condition testing, because development gates nothing (multiple_testing.development_screen) and validation breakpoints use validation sessions only (tercile_rule.breakpoints). If every development year is dropped, development is reported as not computed and every item is underpowered there. (The former condition of at least 2 development years was left over from the removed development gate; review round 7, C13.)
coverage_rule.dropped_year_consequences: (a) Breakpoints: a dropped year's sessions are skipped, and a dropped year's events never enter a trailing window. (b) Segments: each edge of a dropped year is a segment boundary under chronology.boundaries, with censoring and, after it, the embargo. (c) Bootstrap: the stage's kept sessions are concatenated in date order, and the circular block bootstrap wraps over that kept list. Each has a synthetic test with a dropped middle year.
coverage_rule.limitation: The coverage stamps sample the whole $1+ universe, not movers, so mover quote coverage may be lower. Per-stage no-entry, terminal and excluded counts are reported so that this is visible.
coverage_rule.decided_by_code: Nobody applies year_rule or item_rule by hand. The count-only code computes each year's three rates and emits the kept or dropped decision per year and the item_rule result. It is bound to its whole specification, not to this object alone (review round 8, F04). The governing count run records in its entry of exposure_registry.run_entries: (1) spec_sha256, the sha256 of the UTF-8 of json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False), where p is this protocol file without the metadata-only paths below; (2) the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/ it ran from; (3) input_manifest_sha256, the sha256 of its input manifest, which lists the sha256 of each pre-freeze snapshot part (0-3) and of the canonical JSON of the 2016-2020 session rows of data/session-calendar.json, the only calendar rows the count reads (so regenerating the calendar with a later end for a later freeze keeps the binding). The run entry is committed and pushed before any person opens the output's rates. The freeze is refused unless the frozen protocol's spec_sha256, the frozen study_code tree and the input manifest recorded in freeze_record equal those of the governing count run. Metadata-only paths, the only ones that may differ between the governing count run and the freeze: $.status; $.frozen_before_outcomes; $.freeze_record (null until the freeze); the status field of each $.freeze_acceptance.items entry; and append-only additions to $.exposure_registry.already_looked_at, $.exposure_registry.run_entries and $.review_record (earlier elements unchanged) and to the text of $.exposure_registry.draft_author_exposure (its earlier value a prefix of the new one). Any other change after the rates are viewed, including a change to a definition the rates depend on (sampling, populations, official prints, quotes, identity) or to the study tree, cannot be frozen under this protocol version; a new version records the seen rates in its exposure registry. A synthetic test changes one non-metadata field, the tree and one snapshot hash in turn and asserts each freeze refusal, and accepts a protocol whose only changes are on metadata-only paths.

tercile_rule.breakpoints: For an event decided on session s, the breakpoints are the 1/3 and 2/3 empirical quantiles (numpy 'linear' method) of MAX21 over all D events with a defined MAX21 whose decision session lies in the 252 kept sessions strictly before s. Every D event counts, whether it entered, had no entry or had no fill. Every input is known at the decision. For an event of the validation stage, the window is restricted to validation sessions strictly before s, so no survivorship-limited development or warm-up event sets a validation breakpoint.
tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints: For a holdout event, the trailing window is the 252 most recent sessions before s that lie outside the gap from 2026-01-02 to N0 - 1. That gap covers #162's reserved holdout, which v3 never reads, and every session from 2026-09-21 to N0 - 1. The window therefore draws only on (a) the sessions ending 2025-12-31 (v1/v2 validation, already exposed), whose membership comes from pre-freeze snapshot part 2, and whose per-event MAX21 lookbacks and DV_reg minute bars (asof = t) are fetched under the first granted 'count' entry, and (b) earlier holdout sessions. It reads covariates and membership only, never an outcome. A synthetic test computes the breakpoints for the first holdout session from part (a) alone.
tercile_rule.assignment: Low if MAX21 <= the 1/3 breakpoint, high if MAX21 > the 2/3 breakpoint, middle otherwise. A value equal to a breakpoint goes to the lower tercile.
tercile_rule.minimum: If fewer than 60 prior D events lie in the trailing window, the event is unassigned: it is counted and reported, and it enters neither H1 item. The 2016 warm-up year supplies the first development window. Validation events of early 2020 stay unassigned until 60 prior validation events accrue; they are counted.

holdout.window: 252 sessions (session_calendar) starting at session N0 = the 40th session after the session of the freeze. N0 is fixed by the freeze commit alone. The freeze commit is the first commit reachable from origin/main (first-parent history) in which blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/protocol-core-draft.json has status frozen; the file keeps this path at and after the freeze and is never renamed or moved. The repository squash-merges pull requests, so a commit that exists only on a PR branch is never the freeze commit. Its committer timestamp, converted to America/New_York, is the freeze time. The session of the freeze is the first XNYS session whose scheduled open is at or after the freeze time. D decisions made on session N0 - 1 enter on N0 and belong to the holdout. Development and validation run by committed automation started at the freeze. The commit that adds the validation results file (with its sha256 in the run log) must be reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on session N0, measured by the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable (the pull request's merged_at, or the push event for a direct push). If it is not, the holdout of this protocol version is void for every item; a new protocol version is required. There is no deferral.
holdout.extension: If any carried item is below its minimum holdout sample after 252 sessions, in observations or in occupied sessions (minimum_sample; for H1-D, in either group), the holdout is extended in 63-session blocks, at most 2. The window is common to every carried item. A carried item still below its minimum after the second block is labelled underpowered. Each extension decision is made by the committed automation, from one 'count' whose unit is count_unit, never an exit or outcome price.
holdout.count_unit: Integers only, keyed as follows: 'H1-D:high' and 'H1-D:low' (one per group, since H1-D is a difference test), 'H1-D-b_lane-low', 'H3-a', 'H3-b' and 'H3-c'. Each key carries n, its observations, and sessions, its occupied entry sessions (for H3-c, occupied t+1 sessions). Count eligibility is final analyzability (review round 8, F05): an observation is counted exactly when it enters the item's primary statistic. For a tradable cell or an H1-D group, that is a trade that passes membership, dedup and every exclusion (including unresolved ticker reuse, exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.identity_probe), meets every rule of chronology.boundaries, has the tercile the key needs, has an entry fill quote inside the entry timeout and filled notional >= $1,000, has a daily bar in both adjustments on its entry session, is not excluded by an in-hold record rule over (e, E] (the split mismatch of populations.suspected_unadjusted_split, and the non-cash and unrecorded distributions of populations.corporate_actions), and has no fetch-incomplete window among its entry quote window and its exit and terminal-search quote windows (populations.fetch_failures). Its exit price is irrelevant: terminal exits stay in the statistic (populations.terminal_exits), a terminal-merger bid always exists, and nothing after E can exclude it (populations.formulas, F_acc). For H3-c, it is an event that meets chronology.boundaries, has all 8 official legs present, a daily bar in both adjustments on each session from t+1 to t+4, and no split mismatch, non-cash or unrecorded distribution in t+2 .. t+5. Only presence, eligibility, timestamp and fetch-status flags, decision-time inputs (MAX21, med20, the entry bar), corporate-action records and the factors a(s) and q(s) (ratios of two closes of one session, never a return) are evaluated. No mid, spread, return or exit value is computed or emitted. At development, validation and the holdout read, count_unit is computed on the same sealed data as the statistic, so it equals the statistic's n and occupied sessions. A holdout 'count' fetches no exit-side quote window, so there every such window counts as complete; the read recomputes count_unit, and that count governs the minima and the MDE. A trade excluded at the read for a fetch-incomplete exit-side window can therefore leave an item underpowered, but no item passes below its minimum. The same unit applies to every minimum_sample check and every MDE at every stage, and the extension rule applies to the smallest key of each carried item. Synthetic tests assert that the count output carries exactly these keys with integer n and sessions, that the count path calls no price or return function, and, on a fixture that triggers every exclusion, that count_unit equals the observations and occupied sessions entering each item's statistic.
holdout.why_prospective: No retrospective window free of prior mover outcomes remains: 2021-2025 is v1/v2 dev/val, 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-18 is #162's reserved holdout and is exposed at event level, 2017-2026-08-14 is broad-universe exposed at aggregate level, and 2016 is the warm-up.
holdout.accrual_exposure: The primary holdout statistic of every item uses every holdout trade; nothing is excluded for exposure. Paper exposure is recorded only for symbol-sessions in which a paper order was submitted, logged at order time (symbol, session, order id, strategy) in the collection batch's accrual log before any outcome of that trade exists. A holdout trade is paper-exposed if any session from decision t through its exit is such a symbol-session. A holdout trade whose span from decision t through exit includes a late-collected session (holdout_gate.prospective_collection) is also paper-exposed, because that session's accrual log was not committed in time. The result without paper-exposed trades is reported only as a sensitivity. If the paper-exposed fraction of any carried item's holdout trades exceeds 5%, the holdout is labelled contaminated for that item, and the item cannot then be labelled supported (confirmatory).
holdout.holdout_read: A holdout read is exactly this: computing, from data of sessions N0 onward, any v3-defined outcome (an exit price paired with a v3 entry, a forward, net or leg return of a D event, a terminal booking) or any statistic built from one. Only such a computation inside a granted 'read' entry is permitted. A 'count' entry permits count_unit only. The following are not reads: (1) collection under holdout_gate.prospective_collection, including computing a batch's sha256; (2) live paper decisions and orders of any strategy, including the NautilusTrader paper runs and their decision streams, which are exposure and are logged in the accrual log; (3) dashboards and timers that publish metadata only (counts, liveness, freshness); (4) computing D membership without any outcome, by committed code whose output is logged in the accrual log. A synthetic test classifies one example of each case.
holdout.read_timing: The holdout read is mandatory (review round 7, C6). The committed automation requests the 'read' for every carried item within 15 sessions after the last session of the final block (the terminal-search windows of censored trades end at most 5 sessions after it). No person decides it: the authorization is granted by rule unless an evaluator refusal applies, and then it is recorded 'refused' with that refusal. A read whose completion reports failed with no results file may be retried under a new authorization before the deadline, from the same study tree and, if one was sealed, the same input snapshot (run_discipline.once). A read that is not completed with a results file by the deadline, is refused, or is void, and a holdout voided for any reason after the gate opened, are numbered deviations, and every carried item is labelled 'not supported (holdout not read)' with the reason (outcome_reporting.rule). No person and no paper result can delay, skip or cancel the read.

labels.development: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development; screening only; survivorship-limited (names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained corporate action cannot be discovered); descriptive only, so it gates nothing (multiple_testing.development_screen)
labels.validation: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development and the S2 headline the author read; screening only, never confirmatory; the 2020 COVID regime is never dropped; not labelled survivorship-limited on the delisting measure: the broad-universe survivorship measure (known_inactive_or_supplement_last_bar_year_histogram in blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/receipt.json, from the same asset-master and corporate-action sources as universe_and_identity.enumeration) counts 563 names whose last bar falls in 2020, inside the 2021-2025 range of 512-756, against 371 in 2019 and 25-167 in 2016-2018. That is a measured count on entitled sources, not proof of completeness, and it was measured under broad-universe's default-asof requests, so it does not cover what asof = s screening misses. The identity diagnostic decides that part (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.identity_diagnostic): if 2020's identity-unreached rate exceeds 2%, every validation result is labelled identity-limited, with the rate stated. Validation uses no development data: its tercile breakpoints come from validation sessions only (tercile_rule.breakpoints), and no development output is an input (multiple_testing.development_screen)
labels.holdout: prospective; untouched only if the validation results commit was reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on N0, no holdout read preceded a committed granted access-log entry, every holdout count and read ran from the frozen study_code tree or a passing transport deviation of it (run_discipline.study_code, run_discipline.transport_deviations), every collection batch has its committed accrual log, and no carried item's paper-exposed fraction exceeds 5%

chronology.boundaries: Segments are assigned by entry session (for H3-c, by session t+1). A D decision whose entry session (for H3-c, session t+1) lies in no segment, such as a decision on 2020-12-31 (entry 2021-01-04) or on the last kept session before a dropped year, is dropped and counted per stage. A trade whose planned exit falls after its segment's last session is censored: it exits at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on that last session, searching past the segment end if needed (populations.terminal_exits.segment_end), is flagged, stays in its segment's statistics and is reported as a count. H3-b makes no entry on a segment's last session (counted). An H3-c event whose legs cross the segment end is excluded from H3-c and counted. Embargo: every item (H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b, H3-c) gives up the first 6 sessions of validation, and the first 6 kept sessions after a dropped year, as entry sessions (for H3-c, as t+1 sessions). Any position can stay open through E+5, the end of its terminal search (populations.terminal_exits), including an H3-a trade, whose planned exit is on its entry session but whose exit can be delayed through the 5th session after it; 6 sessions keep every censored or delayed position of the earlier segment clear of later entries (review round 8, F10). There is no embargo at N0: the holdout follows years after validation, no v3 trade is open in the sessions before N0 (those sessions are lookback inputs only), and D decisions on N0 - 1 enter on N0. A synthetic test covers the embargo after development, the embargo after a dropped year, a 5-session trade entered on N0 that is kept, an H3-a trade entered on the last development session whose exit is delayed into validation, and the first H3-a entry allowed after the embargo.

labels.passes_stage: The item passes its stage rule. The pass has a stage-specific name: 'development pass' at development (descriptive only; it gates nothing, multiple_testing.development_screen), 'screened' at validation (Holm in the 5-item family, the minimum sample and, for a tradable cell, the robustness means), and 'supported (confirmatory)' at the holdout (the same rule, and for H3-c the validation sign of multiple_testing.no_direction_lock). Only the holdout label is a claim.
labels.not_supported_mde_excluded: The stage has at least its minimum sample, the item does not pass, and the one-sided bootstrap-percentile confidence bound (from the same B draws, numpy 'linear' quantile) at Bonferroni level a = 0.05/5 = 0.01 excludes an effect of the preregistered MDE for the realized n (minimum_detectable_effect). For the alternative 'less than 0' (H1-D), the bound is the a-quantile of the bootstrap statistics, and the MDE is excluded when that bound is greater than -MDE. For the alternative 'greater than 0' (every tradable cell), the bound is the (1 - a)-quantile, and the MDE is excluded when it is less than +MDE. H3-c is two-sided at every stage: it uses a = 0.05/10 and requires both conditions, the lower bound (the a-quantile) greater than -MDE and the upper bound (the (1 - a)-quantile) less than +MDE. The fixed Bonferroni level is used because Holm's step-down level is not defined for items after the first retained hypothesis.
labels.underpowered: The stage is below its minimum sample, or the stage is void (populations.fetch_failures), or its test is degenerate (statistics.degenerate), or the item neither passes nor excludes the MDE.

outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict: Primary-hypothesis and profitability verdicts are separate (review round 8, F07). Each is computed per stage (development, descriptive; validation, the screening verdict; the holdout, the confirmatory verdict for a carried item) from one item's label only. (1) H1 verdict, the claim that high-MAX21 D movers underperform low-MAX21 D movers on the b_lane arm: H1-D's label alone. (2) H3 verdict, the claim that D movers' overnight and intraday official-print legs over t+1 .. t+5 differ in mean log return: H3-c's label alone. (3) Three profitability verdicts, one per tradable cell, each supporting only that its own trade has a positive mean net return after costs: H1-D-b_lane-low (low-MAX21 b_lane), H3-a (a_intraday) and H3-b (b_overnight). A profitability pass supports no primary hypothesis: a profitable low-MAX cell is not evidence that high-MAX underperforms low-MAX, and a profitable a_intraday or b_overnight trade is not evidence that the legs differ. A primary pass implies no profitability, since H1-D and H3-c are not tradable. Each verdict takes its item's label (a pass by its stage name with its qualifiers, not supported with the excluded size, underpowered, or 'not supported (holdout not read)'). At the holdout an item that was not carried has no holdout verdict and is reported as 'not carried', and its validation verdict stands as a screening result. A report states each verdict with its exact claim above and never merges them into a hypothesis-level pass.
outcome_reporting.validation_reporting: Every item receives its validation p and enters the validation Holm run, whatever its development result. Development is survivorship-limited, so it nominates nothing and never removes an item from validation or the holdout. An item scores p = 1 at validation only when it is not tested (coverage_rule) or validation is void (populations.fetch_failures, run_discipline.deviations). The H1 high and middle b_lane cells are reported descriptively at every stage, with no p-value.
outcome_reporting.qualifiers: Contamination, lineage and deviation status are qualifiers attached to a label, never labels of their own. A holdout item that meets the pass rule while its holdout is contaminated is labelled 'screened (contaminated holdout)', never 'supported (confirmatory)'. An item labelled 'supported (confirmatory)' that is not lineage-confirmed (multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity) carries 'lineage-unconfirmed'. A stage whose data were fetched or collected under a transport deviation (run_discipline.transport_deviations) carries 'transport-deviation'. Every development and validation result carries 'retrospective reconstruction' (universe_and_identity.availability), and every development and validation result carries 'identity-limited (ticker reuse unresolved)' when exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.identity_probe leaves ticker reuse unresolved (review round 8, F08 and F09).
outcome_reporting.rule: Only these three labels are used, with the qualifiers above, plus one fixed label: a carried item whose holdout is not read by the deadline, is refused or is void is labelled 'not supported (holdout not read)' with the reason and no excluded size (chronology.holdout.read_timing). A result from a deviated study tree (other than a passing transport deviation) is reported beside the governing result with no label at all. A miss is never reported as 'falsified' or as proof of no effect, and 'not supported' otherwise always states the size it excludes. A result in the direction opposite to a one-sided alternative, or for H3-c at the holdout opposite to the validation sign, is reported descriptively with its estimate and interval and supports no claim.

multiple_testing.family: One family of m = 5 items (item_set): H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b, H3-c. H6 and the deferred H2, H4 and H5 are not in it.
multiple_testing.item_id_rule: item_ids is the complete list, in bytewise ASCII order. That order is used for stream spawning, for the final tie-break and for the validation results file.
multiple_testing.procedure: Holm step-down at family-wise alpha 0.05, applied separately at validation and at the holdout, over these 5 items only. An item not carried to a stage, or not tested for lack of data, scores p = 1 there. The validation results file contains all 5 validation p-values keyed by item_ids (1 only for items not tested); the evaluator refuses an incomplete file.
multiple_testing.no_direction_lock: H3-c's p is two-sided at every stage, with the two-sided p of statistics.p_value in its Holm slot, and no development output sets its direction. The full draft and the first core draft locked H3-c after development to the sign of its development estimate. That lock is removed (review round 6): development is survivorship-limited, and a lock set by a survivorship-biased estimate could stop H3-c from ever validating or reaching the holdout. At the holdout, a confirmatory pass of H3-c also needs the holdout estimate to have the sign of the governing validation estimate (review round 7, C7). Validation is the governing screen and is not survivorship-limited on the delisting measure, and H3-c is carried only if it validated, so that estimate is nonzero. A significant holdout estimate of the other sign is reported descriptively with its estimate and interval and supports no claim. A synthetic test asserts that validation and holdout p-values do not change when every development output is altered, and that a significant holdout H3-c opposite to the validation sign does not pass.
multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze: At the freeze, H1 and H3 are each recorded in freeze_record as either 'data in hand, tested' or 'not tested, p = 1 at every stage, permanently', by coverage_rule. Data from a new source, or a new historical range acquired after the freeze, can support only a new protocol version with its own family (v3.1+), never this family's Holm run. The prospective Alpaca SIP data collected under holdout_gate.prospective_collection are not new data in this sense.
multiple_testing.development_screen: Unadjusted p <= 0.05 with the minimum sample: one-sided in the stated direction for H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a and H3-b, and two-sided for H3-c. Development is descriptive: its pass ('development pass') is reported for every item and gates nothing. Every item goes to validation (outcome_reporting.validation_reporting). No development output (an estimate, a sign, a pass or an event's tercile breakpoint) is an input to validation, the holdout gate or any holdout statistic, because 2017-2019 is survivorship-limited (chronology.labels.development).
multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity: The mover question has already tried 1,012 rule-exits (v1 768, v2 244) and broad-universe-mover-v1's 60 predeclared signal variants on overlapping or other windows. Every validation and holdout p is also reported against Bonferroni 0.05 / (1012 + 60 + 5) = 4.64e-5. The archived 35-item draft computed nothing and is not counted. broad-universe's controls and descriptive lane have no pass rule and are not counted, which is a stated limitation. Each p is reported beside the normal-tail p of statistics.normal_tail_p. With B = 100,000, a bootstrap p at 4.64e-5 means at most 3 null-side draws, so the bootstrap p alone cannot resolve this level. An item is lineage-confirmed only if both its bootstrap p and its normal-tail p are at or below 4.64e-5.
multiple_testing.tie_breaks: Where items tie on a p (for example at the floor 1 / (B + 1)) in Holm ordering or in reporting, ties are broken by the normal-tail p, then by item id in bytewise ASCII order.
multiple_testing.tests_not_in_family: BH (q = 0.10) diagnostics across year, price-tier and tercile splits are reported but can never open the holdout.
